course_outline_concepts: PRM800K (Lightman 2023): step-level labeling protocol + annotation cost
Let's-Verify-Step-by-Step: process vs outcome supervision comparison
Math-Shepherd + OmegaPRM: automated MC step labeling; GSM8K gains
SWE-RL (Meta 2025): rule-based difflib reward as a scalable RL substrate
role_in_track: Fourth content chapter of the RL track (ch-37..ch-46). Follows ch-43 (Entropy Dynamics and KL Control) by swapping the learned reward model for step-level process supervision (PRM) or for a deterministic program-verifier (RLVR / SWE-RL). Sets up ch-45 (Self-Improvement Loops) and ch-46 (Lab: DPO or RLVR).

sources.what_to_extract: Step-level label schema (+1 correct / -1 incorrect / 0 neutral); 800K labels on ~75K solutions over 12K MATH problems; aggregation = product of per-step p_correct (paper) vs min (Math-Shepherd); 78.2% on MATH-500 via Best-of-1860 vs 72.4% ORM vs 69.6% majority; active learning ~2.6x label efficiency; ~10x per-example cost vs outcome labeling.

Process vs outcome head-to-head on MATH-500: PRM 78.2 vs ORM 72.4 vs majority 69.6; PRM curve dominates ORM at every N; PRM highlights the exact bad step in wrong solutions; labeling interface schema (labelers mark one step at a time as positive/negative/neutral).

PRM trains a binary classifier per step (prefix, step) -> {good, bad}; cross-entropy on non-neutral steps only; inference cost ~L forwards (L steps) vs 1 for ORM; calibration superiority of PRM over ORM; active learning ranks unlabeled steps by uncertainty on good/bad head.

Automatic labeling formula MC(s_t) = (1/K) sum I[rollout from s_t reaches gold]; hard vs soft labels; K=8 or 16 completions; PPO reward composition R_total = r_final + lambda * sum PRM(step_t); Mistral-7B GSM8K 77.9 -> 84.1 (+PPO) -> 89.1 (+verify); MATH 28.6 -> 33.0 -> 43.5; min aggregation beats prod and mean; soft wins on MATH.

Divide-and-conquer MCTS reduces rollout count from O(L*K) to O(K*log L); threshold tau ~ 0.2; soft MC regression target; 1.5M step labels on ~80K problems; Gemini Pro MATH 51.0 -> 69.4 with PRM-weighted best-of-N; K >= 16 recommended; ~100K TPU-hours.

Formal RLVR: r(x,y) = v(x,y) in {0,1}; verifier domains (math sympy/exact-match, IFEval regex, code unit tests in sandbox); PPO settings LR 1e-6, beta_KL 0.04, clip 0.2, GAE lambda 0.95, gamma 1.0 (episodic); no proxy RM -> no Goodhart gap; prompt curation rule: only prompts with a verifier + gold answer enter RLVR set; verifier-engineering risk (string-match loopholes).

Tulu 3 RLVR block: LR 3e-7, beta (KL) 0.05, clip epsilon 0.2, K=4 PPO epochs, N_mb=1, GAE 0.95, gamma 1.0, local mini batch 32, local rollout 32, total episodes 10,000,000; measured gain +5-10pp GSM8K, +~4pp IFEval; SFT -> DPO -> RLVR three-stage pipeline; released 8B/70B/405B.

Rule-based reward r = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, pred, gold).ratio() in [0,1]; 11M issue-PR triples; GRPO group size G=8, KL beta 0.02, LR 1e-6; Llama3-SWE-RL-70B 41.0% SWE-Bench Verified; out-of-domain transfer to HumanEval+ (+6), MATH (+4), BBH (+3); continuous reward beats binary thresholding; no unit-test execution during training.

Origin of sample-and-rank for reasoning: generator + outcome verifier > generator-only finetuning; GSM8K dataset (8.5K problems); verifier training on 100 sampled completions per problem, 1 epoch; coverage argument (generator must not overfit); this paper is the ORM precursor PRM800K displaces.

Step-level granularity also helps preference optimization, not just reward modeling; Step-DPO loss shares DPO functional form but uses (prefix, good-step, bad-step) triples; Qwen2-7B MATH 53.0 -> 58.6 with 10K step-pref pairs, beating full-trajectory DPO on 100K pairs; motivates why per-step credit assignment matters beyond PRMs.

Counter to 'RL only sharpens priors' critique: prolonged RL + KL control + reference-policy resets + task diversity can expand the reasoning boundary; justifies investing in verifier-engineering + long RLVR runs rather than writing off RL after saturation.

Pass@k critique: RLVR often improves pass@1 while base wins at large k; read it as a calibration on claims about RLVR + PRM gains; track both pass@1 and pass@large-k when evaluating verifiable-reward runs.

deliverables: read.md (220-280 lines, content format with PRM800K label protocol, lets-verify PRM-vs-ORM table at {MATH-500, GSM8K}, Math-Shepherd MC formula, OmegaPRM divide-and-conquer analysis, RLVR hyperparameter block, SWE-RL difflib reward)

figures/prm-vs-orm.html (self-contained interactive comparing PRM / ORM / RLVR gains as the learner varies base-model capability and PRM-quality; second panel plots label-cost per 1% eval gain; ~200-280 lines, no CDN)
